in_sanskrit.name: असव:
in_sanskrit.long_meaning: The Sanskrit word 'असव:' (Asav) is derived from the prefix 'अस-' (as) which means 'not' and the suffix 'व-' (v) which denotes absence. It can be interpreted as 'absence of', 'not present', or 'lack of'. In Hindu mythology, the demon Asura (असुर) is also called Asava (असव) because he was the embodiment of 'asav' or absence of divine qualities.

data.cultural_impact: The name Asav is not commonly used in Hindu communities and is more often seen as a traditional name or used in religious contexts. data.spiritual_significance: In Hinduism, the name Asav carries deep spiritual significance as it embodies the concept of ‘moksha’ or liberation from the cycle of birth and rebirth. The name Asav is associated with the Ashtavakra, a legendary sage and philosopher, who was born free from physical and mental afflictions. He is believed to have attained enlightenment at a very young age and is seen as a symbol of self-realization and spiritual perfection. Thus, the name Asav serves as a reminder of the ultimate goal of Hinduism - to attain spiritual freedom and liberation from the cycle of birth and death.

Asav is also the name of a demon king in Hindu mythology, as mentioned in various Puranas. The exact time period of these texts is not definitively known, but they are believed to have been composed between the 2nd century BCE and the 8th century CE.
